question.text: Infosys spot price is Rs. 1,500, risk-free rate is 8% p.a., and the 3-month futures price is Rs. 1,560. The fair futures price is Rs. 1,530. An arbitrageur should:

answer.text: Buy Infosys in the spot market and sell Infosys futures (cash and carry arbitrage)
Sell Infosys in the spot market and buy Infosys futures
Buy both Infosys spot and futures

explanation.text: The Logic: Fair futures price = 1,500 x (1 + 0.08 x 3/12) = Rs. 1,530. Actual futures price is Rs. 1,560, so futures are overpriced relative to the fair value. The cash-and-carry trade is to buy spot at Rs. 1,500 and sell futures at Rs. 1,560, locking in an arbitrage profit of Rs. 30 (after the cost of carry). The Trap: Selling spot and buying futures is the reverse cash-and-carry trade and is used when actual futures price is less than the fair futures price; cash-and-carry is used when actual futures price is higher than the fair futures price. Buying both legs has no arbitrage payoff, and "no opportunity exists" misreads the mispricing.
